precepts.text: He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments. The baptism unto Moses goes back to the commandments, because that represents Christ.
precepts.point: To summarize: Israel needed manna every day to survive the wilderness, and Christ compared that to needing the word of God. I am not saying simply read your Bible. The point is that spiritual life requires consistent, continual nourishment, just as physical life requires continual food. Those of you who think you are ten toes down: when Jacob's trouble magnifies itself, you are going to survive that with this diet? You need to be training all the time for that day. Be the warrior in the garden instead of a gardener in a war. There is a big difference between trials and tribulation; the scripture says we have not yet resisted unto blood.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”. Everybody says the Corinthians were Gentiles. If they were Gentiles, how is it that all their fathers were under the cloud in the wilderness? Reading is fundamental; sometimes it is as simple as that.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. When they try to tell you what baptized means, go to Sirach: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That is Moses being given the commandments in the cloud.

The baptism is the receiving of the laws and the doing of the laws, in the faith of Christ; do not leave that part out, because the whole Bible is about Christ. Moses did not dip the six hundred thousand men and all the rest into rivers. Where was the water? The Lord had to provide water from a rock. It all goes back to the commandments, because that represents Christ.

Then “did all eat the same spiritual meat”: the manna, and the law of life and knowledge. “And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Everything in the wilderness was the foreshadowing, the setup, to show the dependency we would need on Christ. Many were overthrown in the wilderness, not by an enemy but by their own lusts, and the way to avoid lusting after those things is to feed yourself on the word of God daily.

precepts.text: The second account of Aaron's garments: rich garments with breeches, pomegranates and bells compassing him round about, the whole world in the writing of the tribes, and a crown of gold upon the mitre; no stranger ever put them on.
precepts.point: Ecclesiasticus gives the second account of these garments and confirms the breeches under the robe of glory. It also shows the pomegranates and bells compassed him, all around the hem and not four corners only, and that the crown of gold sat upon the mitre before Israel had any kings, because mediator between the Most High and His people is the highest honor; for the brothers given the honor to lead and teach among the nation, do not take it for granted or be slothful in it, for there is nothing more honorable to do on this earth.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
Ecclesiasticus gives the second account of these garments. The Most High “exalted Aaron, an holy man like unto him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi”, made “An everlasting covenant” with him, “and clothed him with a robe of glory.” Under that robe of glory it confirms the breeches: “strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the ephod.”

“And he compassed him with pomegranates, and with many golden bells round about, that as he went there might be a sound”: the pomegranates and bells compassed him, all around the hem and not four corners only. The breastplate of judgment, the Urim and Thummim, and the “precious stones graven like seals, and set in gold” are all here, “with a writing engraved for a memorial, after the number of the tribes of Israel”: the whole world in the writing of the tribes.

“He set a crown of gold upon the mitre, wherein was engraved Holiness”. A crown of gold sat upon the mitre before Israel had any kings, because mediator between the Most High and His people is the highest honor. “Before him there were none such, neither did ever any stranger put them on, but only his children and his children’s children perpetually.”

For the brothers given the honor to lead and teach among the nation: do not take it for granted or be slothful in it, for there is nothing more honorable to do on this earth.

precepts.text: The everlasting covenant of the priesthood with Aaron and his seed: to offer the sacrifices and to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws.
precepts.point: That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: “Moses consecrated him, and anointed him with holy oil: this was appointed unto him by an everlasting covenant, and to his seed, so long as the heavens should remain, that they should minister unto him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and bless the people in his name.” That is the perpetual statute of the priest's office to Aaron and his sons.

The Most High “chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense, and a sweet savour, for a memorial, to make reconciliation for his people.” And He gave him “his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Israel in his laws.”

So the priest's job was two things: the offerings, and teaching the nation the law, statutes and commandments.

precepts.text: Phinehas is third in glory for his zeal, and the covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood was his reward.
precepts.point: These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one man brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of all: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. Phinehas saw it and rose up.

“The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart: when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.” Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.

“Therefore was there a covenant of peace made with him, that he should be the chief of the sanctuary and of his people, and that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever.” The javelin that stayed the plague from the children of Israel won him the covenant of peace and the priesthood for ever.

precepts.text: Aaron was chosen to offer sacrifice and make reconciliation, and to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in his laws.
precepts.point: That is why Levi had no land of their own but dwelt among all the tribes of Israel: they were responsible for making the sacrifices and teaching the laws to the people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.” This is the office the Most High gave Levi, and in particular the high priest. Ecclesiasticus says it of Aaron: “He chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense, and a sweet savour, for a memorial, to make reconciliation for his people.”

And the teaching came with the office: “He gave unto him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Israel in his laws.” Sacrifice, incense and reconciliation on one side, teaching Jacob the testimonies and informing Israel in his laws on the other, and both pertained to Aaron's lineage. That is why Levi had no land of their own but dwelt among all the tribes of Israel: they were responsible for making the sacrifices and teaching the laws to the people.

precepts.text: Phinehas' zeal made reconciliation for Israel and gave his seed the dignity of the priesthood forever.
precepts.point: Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart: when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.” This is the same standing up the psalm records: when the people had turned back to Baal–peor, Phinehas stood up, executed judgment, and the plague was stayed. His zeal made reconciliation for Israel.

“Therefore was there a covenant of peace made with him, that he should be the chief of the sanctuary and of his people, and that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever”. That is what “counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore” means: his zeal in the fear of the Most High gave his seed the dignity of the priesthood forever.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: Read for the complete thought: the Lord “made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.” Out of Jacob, out of the twelve tribes, came Moses.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: What tribe was Moses from? “These are the families of Levi according to their generations. And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses.” Moses was a Levite, and his father’s name was Amram. Note it down for the lineage.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “And the name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi”; “and she bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.” Miriam, Moses and Aaron were brothers and sister, the children of Amram, and their mother was Jochebed. Write it under lineage.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The estimated time of Moses’ birth: “Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.” Write down about 1526 BC; other estimates place it in the 13th to 14th century BCE, with a traditional date of 1393 BCE. These are approximates, placed by which pharaohs were ruling at that time.

“But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.” Ain’t that us? Look at us now: the more we get afflicted, the more we multiply. Moses was born into that affliction, when the Egyptians “made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick”.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
“There went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.” She hid the goodly child three months, laid him in an ark of bulrushes in the flags, and his sister stood afar off. Pharaoh’s daughter found him, and his sister asked, “Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women”, and the maid “called the child’s mother.” Look how the Lord set that up. Everything is by design.

When Moses was grown “he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens”, and seeing an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, “he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.” He stood up for his people, and his own people used it against him: “Who made thee a prince and a judge over us?” Word got back to Pharaoh, and Moses had to flee to Midian, where he was about forty years. But he returned.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
It was Moses whom the Lord used to lead the Israelites out of Egypt: “Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.” Moses said, “Who am I”, and the Lord said, “Certainly I will be with thee.”

And when they ask his name: “I AM THAT I AM”; “Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” That is who sent him.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
This was after all hell had broken loose. After all the plagues hit, Pharaoh “called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people”; “take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone”. The Egyptians were urgent to send them out in haste, “for they said, We be all dead men.” And Israel “borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment”.

So Moses rose up out of captivity, born in affliction, stood up for his people, and the Lord used him. He did not care about being comfortable in Egypt, and he was high up there, not some Joe Schmo. He loved his people more.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
“By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid”, because “they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.” They chose to do what God said.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. Read that to the negro who says we ain’t slaves, I’m getting money, I don’t feel no racism. Read it to the apologists who will sell out their own heritage, the truth of who their people are, to appease somebody else, saying that would start a race war.

“Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.” He knew better things were coming. “By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king”: he was not fearful of what would happen to him for forsaking Egypt.

In Christianity our people learned nothing of their forefathers, and you can see they lack all manner of faith: they won’t give up anything that lessens their pockets, and are willing to sell their soul to keep the riches of Egypt.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: Moses met with the Lord on Mount Sinai, where he received the Ten Commandments. “And the Lord came down upon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the Lord called Moses up to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.” The people were charged not to break through “unto the Lord to gaze, and many of them perish.” “Thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee”: only they could come up.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “And God spake all these words, saying, I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me.” Here the Lord gives the commandments to Moses. And don’t think everything from verse 1 down to 17 took forty days; a lot happened within that time frame.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
“And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking”. Imagine being at the bottom of the mountain, Moses and Aaron gone up to the top, and you looking up at lightning and thunder, a trumpet sounding and the mountain on fire. They backed on up and stood afar off, because they didn’t know what was taking place up there.

“Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die.” They understood the power that was up on that mount. “And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.”

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
A historical point: it was through Moses that the Red Sea was parted. The Bible games ask, Who parted the Red Sea: Noah, Jesus, Mary or Moses? and the Christians are perplexed.

“And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.” “And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.”

This book is your history book. It is yours exclusively, and everybody is trying to take it from you. Malcolm X and Marcus Garvey tried to instill in us a pride in our ancestors, because our ancestors would give us a vision of how to walk in the midst of enemies. Being cut off from that left us with no vision as a people, and look how our kids and our men have turned out, with no direction. Read this Bible with new eyes, pick out the details, and walk like your forefathers, and watch us become a better nation, men and women.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
“And where water stood before, dry land appeared”. We think of the parted sea as muddy. No: dry land appeared, “and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field”. They were walking on grass, a flat, perfect path, not a rock or a boulder. The water stood on both sides and in the middle a perfect green path. You never felt VIP until you walked through the Red Sea: always counted as trash by the Egyptians, and now VIP.

“Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders.” The Lord was with them and they saw all the strange wonders. Reading this makes you ask how they got to the other side and started bugging out. “They went at large like horses, and leaped like lambs”, and they were “mindful of the things that were done while they sojourned in the strange land”: they remembered how “the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle”, and how the river cast up frogs.

“For quails came up unto them from the sea for their contentment.” And the sinners “suffered justly according to their own wickedness”. We were meant to be there; the Lord knew it was going to happen regardless.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
While in Midian, God appeared to Moses in a burning bush. Moses “came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb. And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush”. “The bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed”: that is confusing, let's just be honest: a bush aflame but not burnt up. At that point Moses knew something different was taking place.

“God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses.” “I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.” He knew what time it was.

“I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows”. Moses had been gone a long time, and out of nowhere the Lord appears and reminds him of his people still back there. Moses felt that; he had fled because of what he did for his people.

Many of us were called out of all walks of life, and not when we would have liked. You were called at the precise moment you were meant to come in. Moses was very old, and he was called. Don’t think you missed out: you came in the way you are so you can exhort somebody, old or young, who is going through what you have been through.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The third point: Moses was not allowed to enter the promised land. The Lord said “speak ye unto the rock before their eyes”, but Moses said, “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?” and “with his rod he smote the rock twice”. “Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.”

Did Moses part the Red Sea? It was the Lord; the Lord used Moses. Everything was of the Lord, and the Lord checked Moses for this. We easily think it is us. You ain’t nobody: whatever your seat, position or title, we are all the same, all striving for the kingdom. Be careful what you say and how you move, because the Lord will sit you down for vain glory. Even in your frustration with a rebellious people, even when someone is back to the same old nonsense and you don’t want to pick up the phone, the Lord made you a counselor for a reason. It is much bigger than any one person.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
“And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo”, “And the Lord shewed him all the land of Gilead, unto Dan”. Something miraculous happened: all that land was not simply visible from the mountain; the Lord showed it to him. “I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.”

“So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.” “Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.” He died strong. Give it up to our forefather Moses, Moshe.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “And Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.” Fourscore is 80, and fourscore and three is 83. Aaron was the older brother by about three years.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
Aaron was born right along with Moses and grew up in the same area. “Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well.” He was very instrumental in what happened in Egypt; Aaron could talk very well.

“And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.” That was the place Aaron played with Moses: his spokesman.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
Write this down: Aaron was the first high priest of the Levitical order. “And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him”, “that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office”. “And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.”

“And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.” The next time they make fun of our garments and call us Power Rangers, show them this scripture and ask if they can laugh at the priesthood. Two onyx stones were graven with the names of the children of Israel, six on each, “for stones of memorial”, and “Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord upon his two shoulders for a memorial.”

The breastplate of judgment had four rows of stones, set in their right order, with a purpose for each one: “the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve”. Each tribe had a stone, and each stone represented something.

It is very descriptive of how the priests were dressed. It was a serious garment, not something to be played with or mocked. They mock our culture because they hate God, and therefore they hate his people; they call a superhero’s cape and colors dope, and a church hat like a satellite dish passes, but they mock us. Don’t let anybody make you feel some type of way about how we move. We roll like our forefathers.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
“And he poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head, and anointed him, to sanctify him.” Moses “anointed the tabernacle and all that was therein”, sprinkled the altar “seven times”, and “anointed the altar and all his vessels”. See how precious this oil is. That is the precious ointment that ran down Aaron’s beard.

Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons and put coats on them. Aaron was very instrumental in the priesthood: the first high priest of the Levitical order. We know about Melchizedek, but in the Levitical order Aaron was number one, and his sons came after him.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity! It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard”. That is how precious the anointing oil poured on Aaron was.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The golden calf. “When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount”, they gathered to Aaron. We are an impatient people, and Israel to this day hates waiting.

“Break off the golden earrings”: Aaron was there for so much, and he fell to what we call peer pressure, a whole impatient nation pressing on him in the middle of nowhere. Remember where those earrings came from: they took all that from the Egyptians on the way out, walking out blinged up. Aaron made the molten calf, built an altar, and proclaimed “To morrow is a feast to the Lord.” He participated in it. When we left Egypt we were messed up; that is why only two made it to the promised land.

“And rose up to play”: they started fornicating. All manner of wickedness we learned in Egypt, they followed. Imagine us getting to the other side and saying, make us something to worship, we want a Christmas tree, crosses to bow to, and then doing what they do at Mardi Gras, tossing beads and gyrating in the street. That is how they worship their gods.

“It is a stiffnecked people”, a hardheaded people. “Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them”. We say Jesus take the wheel; you don’t understand what happens when he gets behind the wheel.

But watch what our forefather did: “And Moses besought the Lord his God”, “Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people. Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants”. That is the spirit of Moses. “And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.” He had respect to Moses’ words. Thank the Lord for our forefather Moses. Had it been one of us, we would have stood aside as the Lord said and started all over, like the reset button on the Nintendo. Imagine coming down from the mountain and everybody is twerking around a molten calf, the same people that just walked out of Egypt and saw all those wonders. That is what we have to learn: the spirit of Moses, who loved his people and pleaded for them.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: Aaron’s rod. “Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent.” It was Aaron’s rod, his staff. The magicians of Egypt did the same with their enchantments, “but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.” Even though theirs turned to serpents too, you saw who overpowered who.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
That same rod. “Thou shalt write Aaron’s name upon the rod of Levi”, and “the man’s rod, whom I shall choose, shall blossom: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Israel”. Twelve rods were laid up before the Lord, and on the morrow “the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.” That is miraculous: the staff had been cut off from its tree a long time, and overnight it budded.

“Bring Aaron’s rod again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels”, “that they die not.” It was a token and a remembrance for those that murmur and have little things to say: remember Aaron’s rod that budded, because you could have died.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The death of Aaron. “Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah.” The Lord was reminding them, because Aaron was there too.

“And strip Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son”; “and Aaron died there in the top of the mount”. “They mourned for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.”

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The Lord used Aaron as high priest, but Aaron’s life was full of mistakes, turmoil and tribulation. He started off a slave just like us and caught hell throughout his life, ups and downs. But at the end of the day he believed and he corrected himself. That is a testimony of our life: we mess up, but we have to take the correction and get back up. And our decisions and mistakes come with long-term effects: because of what he did, Aaron did not see the promised land in this life.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” We go back to these accounts to remember who we are, and to remember what to do in these situations. We laugh at them going right back to the same nonsense, but we do the same thing whenever we fall to temptation, lust, or whatever demon is housed inside us: going right back to Egypt when we know better. Give it up for our forefather Aaron, tribe of Levi.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The account of the coup. Korah, the son of Levi, “and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men”, two hundred and fifty princes, “And they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron”. “Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy”: everybody is holy, the Lord is with all of us. Watch brothers who come in trying to set themselves in positions and titles. There is order and structure here; we don’t do things willy-nilly.

“Even to morrow the Lord will shew who are his, and who is holy”. “Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.” These were sons of Levi, separated to do the service of the tabernacle, “and seek ye the priesthood also?” Folks come in wanting to be the HNIC, but that is not how the Lord does things. Dathan and Abiram called Egypt “a land that floweth with milk and honey”, complaining without realizing order and structure, and “Moses was very wroth”: Moses was pissed. “Respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them.”

“Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.” “And they fell upon their faces”: “shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation?” That is how you know Moses loved his people: going through all this with them, he still spoke up. “Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest ye be consumed in all their sins.” Their wives, sons and little children stood with them.

“If these men die the common death of all men”, the Lord had not sent Moses. “But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up”, then they would understand. As soon as he stopped speaking “the ground clave asunder”, and “They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them”. A new thing: no coincidence, no natural disaster. God opened the earth, took them, and closed it. Even the little children went; you say, not my Jesus.

Things written aforetime were written for our learning. Pay attention to how the Lord deals with murmurers and people out of order who bring dysfunction: they all have to go. We have seen the tree get shook in here, and everybody connected to them had to go. It is like pitch: touch it and you are defiled. Make sure you are not the plague, because the Lord will open the earth up and your whole clique has to go.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
In Numbers 16 they challenged Moses’ and Aaron’s leadership and refused to acknowledge what God said. The Reubenites: “This is that Dathan and Abiram, which were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord”.

“And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died, what time the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men: and they became a sign.” It was a sign for Israel. That murmuring, upset and mad: let it go, or the earth will open up on you. “Notwithstanding the children of Korah died not.”

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “And Eleazar Aaron’s son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas: these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their families.” Phinehas was the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
This is what Phinehas is known for. A man of Israel brought a Midianitish woman “in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation”, and Phinehas “took a javelin in his hand”, “and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.” You can’t erase this or say it didn’t happen. “Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.”

Why? “The people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” They ate of the sacrifices of their gods and bowed down, “And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.” The Lord was mad with Israel. “Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.” You say, not my Jesus? And Moses was a meek man; this is meekness. Moses heard that commandment and said, “Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.” Some think Phinehas was just crazy. No, he was following orders. That many died for joining themselves to idols: the Lord is nothing to play with.

“Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them”. “Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace”, “even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.” That is what we read in Sirach. God was not mad at Phinehas; Phinehas followed orders. The man of Israel slain with the Midianitish woman was Zimri, “a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.”

A disclaimer for the Levites: you cannot do that anymore. Do not pick up a javelin and say you slew someone in the name of the Lord because you have zeal.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
The Lord gave us commandment not to deal with the other nations: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” People get upset, but you can’t erase it or make it seem God ain’t like this.

“For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. It is not a question of if; they will. Even King Solomon fell. You think you are special? You know better than the Lord? “So will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.”

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: Phinehas led Israel in battle against the Midianites. “Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites”: a thousand of every tribe, “twelve thousand armed for war.” “And Moses sent them to the war, a thousand of every tribe, them and Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, to the war, with the holy instruments, and the trumpets to blow in his hand.” They slew all the males and the “five kings of Midian.” Phinehas was there in that battle.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why:
Another part of his office. Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh “built there an altar by Jordan, a great altar to see to”, and all Israel gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them. And they sent “Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, And with him ten princes”. Phinehas was about the business; he was no regular dude.

“What trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to turn away this day from following the Lord”? “Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we are not cleansed until this day”? Go back and read the rest of the chapter. Studying according to individuals, there is a lot of history recorded.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “And Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days”, before the ark of the covenant, asking “Shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the Lord said, Go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand.” Phinehas continued as the high priest even in Judges.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

precepts.why:
“For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness”: the light that shined out of darkness is Christ. God commanded Christ to shine out of darkness, meaning he created Christ.

That light “hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.” In the face of Jesus Christ you can see the glory of God. What Moses and all of us were seeing, that shine Moses was seeing when he saw Christ: that glory is the glory of God.

Read on: “But we have this treasure”. Esdras also talks about that treasure: that light is that treasure. So the glory of God that Moses saw is the light that shines and emanates from Christ. That is the part of his glory Moses was shown.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

precepts.why:
Christ is the one “Who is the image of the invisible God”. Christ is the image of his Father, so if you see Christ’s glory, whose glory is he? In Revelation it tells you both of them is a light. If you see the glory of Christ you see the glory of the Father.

That is why the glory Moses saw was Christ’s, and still it is called the glory of God: because the Father is invisible, nobody has ever seen him, and Christ is his image.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

precepts.why:
Christ made it clear for anybody that has questions: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time”. Nobody ever heard the voice of Christ’s Father, at any time. No matter if you are going to read something about thus saith the Lord, the Lord God the Almighty: it is not him, not Christ’s Father. Christ knows, so he is letting us know. It’s simple like that.

“Nor seen his shape.” He had to put emphasis on the shape, because they are saying the shape Moses saw in the wilderness is the Father. No: I showed Moses the glory of me, and I am the image of the invisible God. The invisible God means nobody ever saw him; that is why he is called an invisible God.

“And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not. Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” Everything you read about, Christ is saying that is me. The voice you heard, that was me; the back you saw, that was me; the scriptures testify of me. Thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, the Lord of hosts: a lot of you thought Isaiah 6 was the Father. No, that’s the Lord, that’s Christ.

“And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.” “But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you.” “I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only?”

“Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.” Moses is the one accusing you; Christ doesn’t have to. That is why he said nobody ever heard the voice and nobody ever saw the shape: he understood they trusted in Moses and the law, and the law says Moses heard the voice of God and saw part of God’s glory. Christ is fixing all of that now: that was never the Father. Nobody ever heard his voice, nobody ever saw his shape.

“For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” It was all Christ Moses was writing about: Israel is my son, even my firstborn. Moses understood it was always Christ. Exodus, Genesis, Deuteronomy, Numbers, Leviticus, the Lord of hosts: that was me Moses was writing about. “But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?”

Read on. That their good things be not abolished. Read on. And that their glory might endure forever. Our job is to lead people to God. And the good things that you learn, that it's not abolished. points: And he brought out of him a merciful man, which found favour in the sight of all flesh, even Moses, beloved of God and men, whose memorial is blessed. A merciful man, to help people that needed mercy. When we were in Egypt, God sent a saviour: Moses.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and shewed him part of his glory.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: Moses, beloved of God, whose memorial is blessed. Moses had his faults, the circumcision matter and speaking unadvisedly so that he did not see the promised land, but God still chose him and his legacy lived on.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: Aaron was given the commandments and authority in the statutes of judgments that he should teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in his laws. That is our job: sisters, cover your head; brothers, rule your house; you cannot eat that. That is how these men got their fame, and they were making people new.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: Phinehas, third in glory, had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage when the people turned back. Stand firm for the laws of God when the people are turning.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things be not abolished and their glory endure forever. You can do this twenty or thirty years and then go off, and you become the example of what not to do.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: Now, let's get the last one. Only God can judge me. A Christian loves to say that so quick. (They got it like they got Tupac on repeat.) Okay, come on. Let's see what the God of the Bible, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob says. Only God can judge me. Only God can judge me. Yo man, y'all got a lot to learn. Let's see what he says about judging.

God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people: Wait a minute. But you can't judge me. You can't judge me. I could do X, Y, and Z according to how I feel or what I think. You can't judge me. But no, the Lord gave the prophets wisdom in their minds to be able to what? Bring forth the righteous will of our Father to their attention. Hey brother, you're going off. That's adultery. That's fornication. According to the scriptures, that's incorrect. You're in sin. We can judge you, but the Lord brings judgement. Our job is just to warn you. Okay? Yo, that's wrong what you're doing. You should not be doing that. Repent. Get yourselves together with the Lord. So, God has given us the understanding of the Bible to do what? To judge his people. I'm not worried about the other nations. He gave me the understanding and wisdom to come and judge the 12 tribes of the children of Israel.
in righteousness: In what? In righteousness. No: for deceit, for filthy lucre, for money? In righteousness.
that their good things be not abolished: That their good things be not abolished. Meaning what? The kingdom.

and that their glory may endure for ever: And that they may have everlasting life with what? The kingdom. Okay, with Christ. That's what we're looking for. We don't want to see y'all lose that opportunity. But a lot of our brothers and sisters are very, very hard-headed.

note.label: What My Pastor Says...

points: This picks up where part one left off, with Moses. Take notes of the key points and the scriptures; and the years given are approximates, always up for debate depending on who you are talking to.
“And he brought out of him a merciful man”: out of Jacob, among whose twelve tribes the heritage was parted, the Lord brought Moses, “beloved of God and men, whose memorial is blessed.”

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “So that his enemies stood in fear of him.” His enemies were the Egyptians. At one point that was his family. But when he woke up to the real fight, the real battle, he found out who his enemies were, and it was not his people; it was the other nations.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “And chose him out of all men”: the Lord chose Moses out of all Israel.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That is Mount Sinai: Moses met with the Lord on the top of the mount and received the Ten Commandments there, and he alone drew near into the thick darkness where God was, while the people stood afar off.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “He exalted Aaron, an holy man like unto him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.” Aaron was the brother of Moses. For his lineage it is the same as Moses: Amram and Jochebed. His estimated birth is around the same, about three years before Moses, his older brother.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “An everlasting covenant he made with him and gave him the priesthood among the people; he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory.” The priest was decked out. When they lie about the Israelites on TV, they make them look like bums in dirty, rent clothes. Read these scriptures and let your imagination go where they take it: Aaron was decked out.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “Before him there were none such, neither did ever any stranger put them on, but only his children and his children’s children perpetually.” You have a lot of strangers trying to be our forefathers right now. It wasn’t for you. Only Aaron’s children and his children’s children were to wear that priestly garment.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “Strangers conspired together against him, and maligned him in the wilderness, even the men that were of Dathan’s and Abiron’s side, and the congregation of Core, with fury and wrath.” This was a coup formed against Aaron in his lifetime: Dathan and Korah.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “And divided unto him the firstfruits of the increase”: there was a purpose behind tithing and the sacrifices, and where that food went. The sons of Aaron ate of the sacrifices, “For they eat of the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave unto him and his seed.” Remember Eli’s sons striking the pot and doing shady things with it: that pot was how the priests ate, and their eating of the sacrifices was according to the law.

To this day our people have no idea what tithing is, what the increase has to do with anything, or who it was for: just, give 10%. Nobody could rise up one day and say, I’m the high priest, give me the tithes; only Aaron’s children could be priests. In the world you never asked why the pastor did what he did; in here you question everything, and that is okay. It is crazy to be a dummy spiritually and an expert in everything else, able to take a car down to the last bolt but not knowing your heritage or how to make it to the kingdom.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “For the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance.” We looked at Aaron’s flaws, the things he did and how he messed up, but the Lord dealt with Aaron.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart: when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.” His estimated birth is likely around 1400 BC, again an approximate.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “Therefore was there a covenant of peace made with him, that he should be the chief of the sanctuary and of his people, and that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever”. Remember where that covenant of peace was made: in Numbers 25.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: “So the inheritance of Aaron should also be unto his seed.” Notice how the Levites always stuck with the southern kingdom, and to this day we rock heavy with Levi.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

points: We talked about our sister Assata Shakur, about Saddam Hussein, even Gaddafi, but remember: ours is the true revolution. The Most High gave us the Bible to do three things. Write this down: increase our knowledge, change our lives, and gather the 12 tribes of Israel.

The first is to increase our knowledge. This is talking about Moses: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That he might teach us his covenants, and the Israelites his judgments.

note.label: Assata & Saddam: a Tale of 2 Revolutions

points: “And he brought out of him a merciful man”: that merciful man is Moses, “which found favour in the sight of all flesh, even Moses, beloved of God”. He was beloved of God, and his memorial is blessed.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.” Pay attention to how high the Lord lifted Moses up.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “By his words he caused the wonders to cease”: by his word, by God’s word. “And he made him glorious in the sight of kings”: he made Moses glorious in the sight of kings. “And gave him a commandment for his people”: he gave Moses the commandments to teach us.

“And shewed him part of his glory.” Who showed Moses part of his glory? Christ is the one, his word: that is who showed Moses part of his glory. People say, see, that was God’s glory, Moses saw God the Father, Christ’s father’s glory. It was not.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud”. The dark cloud is the Chariot. So Moses went into the Chariot and sat with Christ, and Christ taught Moses and showed Moses a lot of things.
Remember what it says: he made him to hear his voice. There is a scripture that says no man ever heard the voice of the Father, so we know this is Christ.
